title: Shorts 2026-10-24
summary: Blanche won't rule out DOJ role in certification; Trump on the DOJ's Alaska suit; Musk, Starlink and Ukraine; CNN barred from Air Force One; Trump's $400M midterm spend.

shorts.title: Blanche on the midterms: "some doomsday scenario" #Shorts
shorts.narration: [serious] Friends, the Attorney General of the United States was asked if the Justice Department might step into how states certify the midterms. Todd Blanche would not rule it out. He said it's not his intent to "improperly interfere with elections," then floated, quote, "some doomsday scenario, for example, right?" [beat] [deadpan] Right. Nothing says "I respect the voters" like a doomsday scenario in the answer. The DOJ also announced its largest team of election observers yet. [beat] [sarcastic] Just the nation's top cop, keeping his options open on counting votes. The Constitution, Article One, Section Four, covers "The Times, Places and Manner of holding Elections for Senators and Representatives," and it never mentions a doomsday scenario. [beat] [incredulous] So, Mr. Attorney General: if you don't plan to interfere, what's the hard part of just saying no? Subscribe. Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: On Thursday, Oct. 22, AG Todd Blanche told reporters he would not rule out DOJ seeking to intervene in states' midterm certification, said it was not his intent to "improperly interfere with elections," and cited a hypothetical "some doomsday scenario, for example, right?"
On Oct. 23 Assistant AG Harmeet Dhillon announced on X that the Civil Rights Division will deploy its largest team of election observers on Nov. 3.

shorts.title: Trump on the DOJ suit over a fake Dan Sullivan: "I'm the one that said, do it" #Shorts
shorts.hook: Trump: "I'm the one that said, do it"
shorts.narration: [amused] Alaska has a Senate race with two Dan Sullivans. One is the senator. The other, Daniel J. Sullivan, filed as a Republican with a near-identical name. Now the Justice Department has sued Alaska over it. [beat] [deadpan] And asked before a Fort Myers rally, Trump said, quote, "I'm the one that said, do it." He called the challenger "the fake." [beat] [sarcastic] Friends, the Justice Department, famously independent, taking orders on the record. Out loud. In Florida. The Declaration of Independence says governments derive, quote, "their just powers from the consent of the governed." Not from the president's say-so about whose name is on the ballot. [beat] [incredulous] And the senator's own campaign said it would, quote, "let the DOJ complaint run its course." MAGA friends: if a Democrat said that about the DOJ, would you call it independent? Subscribe. Dylan Avanti roasts the news from the Left Coast.

claims.text: The Justice Department sued Alaska, its elections director and state election boards over newcomer Daniel J. Sullivan, who filed as a Republican under a similar name, citing voter confusion.
Asked about the suit before a Fort Myers rally, Trump said: "I'm the one that said, do it." He called Daniel J. Sullivan "the fake" candidate.
Sen. Dan Sullivan's campaign spokesman Nate Adams said the campaign would "let the DOJ complaint run its course."
The Declaration of Independence: governments derive "their just powers from the consent of the governed".

shorts.title: Musk: Starlink limits "decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS" #Shorts
shorts.narration: [serious] Ukraine's drones lost Starlink speed on October fourteenth, right when they were hunting Russian attack drones. The Wall Street Journal and CBS report Elon Musk ordered the limits. [beat] [deadpan] Musk's answer on X, quote: "Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS." Secretary of State Rubio told reporters, quote, "There was no foreknowledge." [beat] [sarcastic] So the richest man in the world says the president did it, the president's people say nobody told them, and the Journal reports that Musk and Trump talked about it. Everybody's innocent. [beat] The Constitution says the President "shall be Commander in Chief of the Army and Navy of the United States." Not the guy who owns the satellites. [beat] [incredulous] So who's actually in charge of America's foreign policy: the president, or a man with a rocket company and an X account? Subscribe for the daily news.

claims.text: The Wall Street Journal and CBS News report that Elon Musk ordered limits on Starshield, SpaceX's military version of Starlink; the slowdown began Oct. 14 and hampered Ukrainian interceptor drones, according to President Zelenskyy.
Musk posted on X on Oct. 14: "Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS."
Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters in India: "There was no foreknowledge."
The WSJ also reports that Musk and Trump discussed the decision, with one source saying they talked before the restrictions were imposed.

shorts.title: CNN to the White House: "mistaken, counterproductive, and unlawful" #Shorts
shorts.narration: [amused] The White House lost in court to CNN, so it moved the fight to the airplane. Judge Timothy Kelly blocked Trump's ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico reporters from White House grounds. But CNN says it's been kept off Air Force One at least four times, though it was the scheduled pool network every time. [beat] [deadpan] CNN's lawyer, Theodore Boutrous, wrote the White House that it's "mistaken, counterproductive, and unlawful," and noted CNN had, quote, "uninterrupted access to the Oval Office and Air Force One for 45 years." [beat] [sarcastic] Forty-five years, ended by a policy nobody will admit to. The First Amendment says Congress shall make no law "abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press." [beat] [incredulous] So, MAGA friends: if a Democrat banned Fox from the plane, would you call that a free press? Subscribe. Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: Trump barred reporters from CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House grounds on Sept. 18; Judge Timothy Kelly then issued a preliminary injunction.
CNN's letter says CNN, the scheduled pool network, was denied Air Force One access for trips in September and October (four times in all per its attorney).
CNN attorney Theodore J. Boutrous Jr. wrote that CNN had "uninterrupted access to the Oval Office and Air Force One for 45 years" and called the efforts "mistaken, counterproductive, and unlawful."
The White House has not directly told CNN it is being excluded; the Justice Department did not respond to AP.
First Amendment: "...or abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press;"

shorts.title: Trump: "more than 300 Million Dollars" spent — "my money that I control" #Shorts
shorts.hook: Trump: "This is my money that I control"
shorts.narration: [amused] Eleven days before the midterms, Trump went on Truth Social and said he'll spend more than four hundred million dollars helping Republicans. He wrote, quote, "More than 300 Million Dollars has already been spent." He didn't give a breakdown. [beat] [deadpan] Back in September, though, in the Oval Office, he did say it: "This is money from MAGA Inc. This is my money that I control." [beat] [sarcastic] Friends, the Campaign Legal Center says that claim violates campaign finance rules. Trump calls it his Great Honor. The Constitution says, quote, "No Title of Nobility shall be granted by the United States." But I guess a nine-figure ad budget is close enough. [beat] [incredulous] If voters were really with them, why does it cost four hundred million dollars to ask? Subscribe. Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: In a Truth Social post reported Oct. 20, Trump said he would spend more than $400m to help Republicans, writing "More than 300 Million Dollars has already been spent on Advertising, Direct and Indirect Voter Contact, Rallies,"; he gave no detailed breakdown.
On Sept. 4 in the Oval Office Trump said: "This is money from MAGA Inc. This is my money that I control."
The Campaign Legal Center accused Trump of violating campaign finance rules by claiming control over MAGA Inc.'s spending.
